page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Esv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyperthreading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it contains no GPUs.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores fall within the average range at 2083.98 and 8040.17 respectively. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show strong performance, with gzip compression reaching 33.58 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.92 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show an average of 604.93 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 81.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model scoring in the weak tier at 5.83 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8s_v7 offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The presence of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) provides hardware-level acceleration for vector and matrix operations. This server is suited for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and moderate data processing pipelines.
